Flexible couple seeking a cheap short break

population.allocation: At least one per positive stratum, then largest remainder; individual estimate weight = target segment share / stratum sample count.

sources.title: Cathay Pacific Annual Report 2025 — HK Express operations
sources.supports: Low-cost leisure positioning, Asian destinations and aggregate passenger statistics; not the assumed target-segment weights.

sources.title: Cathay Group December 2025 traffic figures
sources.supports: Aggregate HK Express passenger counts and load factors; no matching membership conversion or segment-share table.

limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Optional-trip interest, recent travel, destination appeal and the appeal of skipping are pre-price private scenario traits, not observed preferences or numerical willingness-to-pay labels.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

rounds.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

decision.reason: The 480 member fare is a genuinely cheap escape that fits my flexible window and the group's bargain-led plans, and I have not had a leisure trip in six months. Although this destination has little particular pull, the low price makes an optional break worthwhile; I would not pay the 600 normal fare if the member quota ran out.

person.segment_label: Flexible friends planning a cheap escape
person.eligibility_reason: This optional leisure departure fits the flexible travel window.
person.travel_party_context: Any companions can use this departure and independently arrange and fund their own tickets; this decision covers one existing member only.
person.booking_trigger: Friends have agreed to be flexible about dates and destination if a cheap escape appears; nobody is obliged to make the trip.
person.departure_time_tolerance: Can adapt to the displayed departure time for a worthwhile deal; no fixed appointment requires this flight.
person.value_context: The group enjoys bargain-led trips and can use this departure. This member chooses and pays only for their own ticket; a weak deal can still be declined.
person.outside_option: Suggest another leisure outing or save for a later trip; do not invent a quoted alternative fare.
person.motivation_context: Keen to arrange an optional break, with no ticket booked and no compulsory date or destination. Has not taken a leisure trip in the last six months. This destination is acceptable but has little particular attraction today. Skipping remains possible, though arranging a worthwhile leisure break is preferred.

analysis.summary: At the 480 HKD member fare, four customers bought and eleven declined. Most declines (eight) cite no ticket both available and within budget, which is an inventory/budget constraint rather than a price objection. Three declines cite low trip or destination interest with a strong outside option, not fare level. Buyers describe the fare as a bargain. Evidence does not support lowering price; the fare is already at its permitted cap, so a higher test is not allowed.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 480 HKD fare on fresh customers will reproduce roughly one-fifth weighted conversion, with declines dominated by availability/budget constraints rather than fare objections; conversion would not materially rise from a lower fare.

analysis.summary: At the current 214 HKD member fare, 13 of 16 customers bought and 3 declined. All three decliners cited low trip interest or a preference to keep schedule and money free, not the fare itself; none objected to price. Buyers repeatedly called 214 a bargain versus the 600 regular fare, and several would still pay regular fare. No inventory denials occurred. Evidence points to strong conversion at the current fare, but buying at 214 does not prove willingness to pay more, and the cap is 480.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce basic-ticket conversion enough to offset the higher per-ticket receipt, because current buyers describe 214 as far below their stated ceilings and several accept the 600 regular fare.

analysis.summary: Of 16 members, 5 bought the 474 HKD member fare and 11 declined. Seven declines were inventory/budget-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), three were low interest or destination appeal, and one was optional-trip browsing. Buyers cited the 474 fare as compelling value versus the 600 normal fare. The current price sits just below the 480 cap. Evidence is mixed: strong value-driven purchases coexist with many environment-forced declines, so a directional price test is weakly supported.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a lower member fare on fresh members will raise conversion among budget-constrained decliners enough to keep basic ticket receipts at least as high as at 474 HKD.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the current 281 HKD member fare, 9 of 16 customers bought and 7 declined. Most buyers cited the fare as a compelling bargain versus the 600 HKD normal fare, though several said they would not pay the normal fare. Decliners mostly had low trip interest or preferred keeping money and schedule free, not a price objection; one was inventory/budget forced. Price is the main driver of purchase, but evidence that higher fares would retain buyers is weak.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not preserve enough purchases to keep basic ticket receipts at or above the current-fare level, because buyers repeatedly anchored on the low fare and declined the normal fare.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the 281 HKD member fare, 7 of 16 customers bought and 9 declined. Four declines were inventory/budget-forced (ENVIRONMENT_FORCED), not price objections. The other five declined for low trip interest, recent travel, or optional-leisure appeal despite calling the fare affordable. Buyers repeatedly cited the fare as a bargain versus the 600 normal fare. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Evidence points to non-price barriers dominating declines, while the low fare drives purchases.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce weighted conversion enough to lower basic receipts, because declines are driven by low trip interest and inventory rather than fare level.

analysis.summary: At the current 283 HKD member fare, 10 of 16 customers bought, citing the fare as a compelling bargain well below the 600 HKD normal fare and within budget. Four declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and two were low-interest casual browsers for whom even a cheap fare was not worthwhile. No customer objected to the price itself. The fare sits well below the 480 HKD cap, and paired metrics suggest higher revenue at the cap, but buying at 283 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will preserve enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts above the current 283 HKD level, since most buyers cited the fare as a bargain far below the 600 HKD normal fare.

analysis.summary: At the current 308 HKD member fare, 8 of 16 customers bought, all citing the fare as a compelling bargain versus the 600 HKD regular fare. Declines split between low trip interest or recent travel (5), unavailable inventory within budget (3), and optional-trip disinterest. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. The paired initial at 480 HKD showed far weaker conversion, suggesting the low fare drives purchases, though buying at 308 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will reduce conversion enough that basic ticket receipts fall below those at the current fare, because buyers repeatedly cite the low fare itself as the decisive purchase driver.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

Five declines were low-interest or optional-trip objections, not price objections; four were environment-forced with no affordable available ticket. No customer objected to the fare itself. analysis.summary: At the current 304 HKD member fare, 10 of 16 customers bought member tickets, generating 3040 HKD in basic receipts, while 6 declined. Most buyers cited the low fare as the decisive trigger and said they would not pay the 600 HKD regular fare. Three declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and three were voluntary-trip objections tied to low interest or recent travel, not price. Capacity is not binding. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers to see whether receipts rise without losing too many buyers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will increase basic ticket receipts relative to 304 HKD, because most current buyers cited the fare as a bargain well below their stated ceilings and would still purchase at a moderately higher price.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

assumptions: Only existing members; no joining or renewal decision and no fee deduction.
Base fares only; all taxes/fuel/add-ons and operating costs excluded. Revenue is not airline profit.
Population weights are explicit scenario assumptions, not measured HK Express market shares.
Fresh stratified members each search round; paired candidate and initial quote in reset, blinded worlds. One seat per member per world.
Only declared public segment/flexibility enter learning; private budgets, motivation and simulator constraints remain environment-only.
Every third round may test a cited LLM direction within a bounded model-scored interval; text never adds a demand label.
Analyst requests allow at most three attempts within the shared call budget. Unavailable analysis supplies no direction; recorded purchases still train Thompson and undergo independent confirmation.
Quoted fares are whole HKD; weighted averages and statistical estimates may have decimals.
Parallel intent elicitation followed by fixed-priority integer inventory clearing; no seat is reserved by an LLM.
Weighted demand estimates and actual panel cash/seat transactions are reported separately.
Final member quotes round down to an amount ending in nine, with any result below HK$30 becoming HK$0; raw search prices remain recorded.
Independent validation compares the formatted initial fallback, formatted selected fare and no offer after freezing both final quotes; no refitting on holdout.
